result.notes: Both PLP pages (womens-clothing-dresses and newarrivals) timed out on networkidle (30s) but rendered successfully — the timeout is caused by long-polling DataCloud/Einstein requests that never settle. Errors are consistent across both pages: React framework warnings (getServerSnapshot caching, defaultProps deprecation), DataCloud c360a.salesforce.com DNS failures (sandbox-only), and Einstein recommendations 403s (sandbox returns 403 in dev). No uncaught exceptions observed. No feature code exists yet so all errors are pre-existing platform noise.

ProductView's internal onAddToCartModalOpen opens the global confirmation modal (no duplicate mount)
Trigger uses isMounted pattern for SSR safety; modal shell gated on isOpen to prevent SSR hooks
quick-view-add-to-cart-btn testid applied via useEffect ref since ProductView creates button internally

contract_deviations: UT-BODY-011/012: Dev session uses addItemToNewOrExistingBasket (single helper from useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper) instead of separate createBasket + addItemToBasket calls. Tests adapted to verify the helper is called with correct product items. Spirit of the tests preserved (verifying basket mutation is invoked correctly).

result.fix_applied: Added 400 Bad Request patterns to BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS in e2e/plp-quick-view.spec.ts
result.root_cause: Einstein recommendation API returns 400 in dev sandbox when basket-mutating actions (add-to-cart) trigger recommendation calls. These errors were not in baseline.json because baseline was captured on page load before any basket mutations existed.

changes.description: Added two regex patterns to BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS: /Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Bad Request)/ and /r: 400 Bad Request/

attempts.errorSummary:
2 test-code bugs found in e2e/plp-quick-view.spec.ts:

1. E2E-003 (line 272): basketErrors regex `/baskets/i` is too broad — it catches `GET /customer/shopper-customers/.../customers/.../baskets -> 400` which is a customer-service read endpoint that returns 400 for anonymous/guest shoppers in the sandbox after SDK cache invalidation. The actual basket mutation succeeded (modal closed, confirmation appeared, product-added row visible). Fix: narrow the regex to exclude the shopper-customers baskets read endpoint, e.g. filter only POST/PATCH on `/checkout/shopper-baskets/` or exclude GET requests to the customer baskets listing endpoint.

2. E2E-006 (line 380): Test assumes add-to-cart button is disabled before selecting a size, but `useProductViewModal` initializes with `initialProduct` from the PLP tile which already has a pre-selected variant (PLP tile products include representedProduct/color selection). ProductView auto-resolves to a valid variant so the button is correctly enabled. Fix: either (a) skip the initial-disabled assertion and only test the OOS path, or (b) find a product that is truly a master with no pre-selected variant (may not exist on this PLP).

E2E-003 console-error budget fails due to missing noise patterns for Einstein API 400 Bad Request errors in BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS (line 22-28 of e2e/plp-quick-view.spec.ts).

When add-to-bag fires, Einstein recommendation API calls return 400 in the dev sandbox — these are known persistent platform noise per baseline volatility tagging rules #8 and #9:
- Rule #8: "r: 400 Bad Request" → persistent, network-sandbox
- Rule #9: "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400" → persistent, network-sandbox

The test's BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS array (lines 22-28) filters 403 errors but NOT 400 errors. The baseline.json didn't capture these because the baseline was taken before any basket mutations existed — Einstein 400s only appear when basket-mutating actions trigger Einstein API calls.

Fix: Add two patterns to the BASELINE_NOISE_PATTERNS array:
  /Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400/,
  /r: 400 Bad Request/,

These match baseline volatility tagging rules #8 and #9 exactly.

E2E-001 fails intermittently with `awaitHydrated` timeout (10s) on cold server start. This is NOT a code defect — the `window.__APP_HYDRATED__` signal in `_app/index.jsx` is correctly implemented (useEffect fires after hydration). Evidence: E2E-001 passed in e2e-runner attempts 1 and 2, failed only in attempt 3. In that same attempt 3, 7 other tests passed — all using the identical `gotoPlp` → `awaitHydrated` flow. No app code changed between attempts 2 and 3.

Root cause: When Playwright's webServer starts a fresh dev server, webpack compilation + SSR + client bundle download + React hydration can exceed the 10s `awaitHydrated` timeout on the FIRST page load. Subsequent tests benefit from warm caches.

Fix options (all in test code/infrastructure):
1. Add a `beforeAll` warm-up hook in the test file that navigates to the PLP once with a longer timeout (e.g., 30s) before any test runs
2. Pass a longer timeout to `awaitHydrated` in the `gotoPlp` helper: `await awaitHydrated(page, { timeout: 30_000 })`
3. Add `retries: 1` in playwright.config.ts for non-CI runs
